spans.s:
Hrada in the Rigveda and later denotes a ‘lake’ or ‘pond.’
Foot notes i. 52, 7; iii. 36, 8; 45, 3; x. 43, 7; 71, 7; 102, 4; 142, 8, etc.
Av. iv. 15, 4; vi. 37, 2; pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xxv. 10, 18; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iv. 1, 5, 12; 4, 5, 10; xi. 5, 5, 8, etc.

Hrade-cakṣus in one passage of the Rigveda is thought by Jackson to mean ‘will of the wisp.’
Foot notes x. 95, 6.
Proceedings of the American Oriental Society, May, 1890, iv.

Hrasva Māṇḍūkeya (‘descendant of Maṇḍūka’) is the name of a teacher in the aitareya Āraṇyaka.
Foot notes iii. 1, 5; 2, 1. 6. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 391. The word must be regarded as a proper name, given from a personal characteristic, much as sthavira is used.

Hrāduni denotes ‘hail’ in the Rigveda and later.
Foot notes i. 32, 13; v. 54, 3.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, vii. 4, 13, 1; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxii. 26; xxvi. 9, etc.
